nodes.description: Long-term prophylactic penicillin is recommended alongside vaccination. The evidence for it is weaker than the recommendation's ubiquity suggests, and the entry records both sides rather than the favourable one: a 21-year two-brother follow-up reports no severe or invasive infection under combined vaccination and prophylaxis, while the 77-patient European registry found no association between prophylactic antibiotic use and subsequent infection risk. The registry also found prescribing varied by country rather than by patient, which is what a practice without a settled evidence base looks like.

nodes.description: C2 is an obligate component of the classical pathway C3 convertase C4b2a. Its absence blocks classical-pathway C3 cleavage, measurable as absent CH50. The lectin pathway converges on the same C4b2a convertase — MASP-2 cleaves C4 and C2 — so its effector arm fails too; only the alternative pathway (C3bBb) remains intact, which is why lysis is preserved and the phenotype is milder than a C3 deficiency.

nodes.description:
Rheumatological disease of any kind, reported in 43% of a 40-patient Swedish C2-deficient cohort. Curated alongside the separately recorded Systemic Lupus Erythematosus rather than instead of it, because the source names SLE as the dominant component but not the whole of it — the two records should not be added together.
What the non-SLE remainder consists of is not curated, and the reason is worth recording. A deep-research report for this disease names Henoch-Schonlein purpura, polymyositis, arthralgia and glomerulonephritis, attributing them to Orphanet. That attribution could not be verified: the cited cohort abstract does not name them, and ORPHA:169147 is not in this repository's reference cache and cannot be built here because the Orphadata bulk XML is not present. The list is therefore left out rather than curated on a report's word.

nodes.description: Pneumococcal, meningococcal and Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccination is the primary preventive intervention, and it works in C2 deficiency for a mechanistically specific reason. C2-deficient individuals mount normal antibody titres — the block is in effector function, not in the humoral response — and those antibodies restore opsonophagocytosis by driving complement activation through the alternative pathway, bypassing the missing C2 step. Vaccination therefore does not repair the classical pathway; it routes around it.
